name: Robin Hood's Bay clifftop
description: Scrub on the steep slope above a Yorkshire fishing village, reached only by lanes too tight for big lorries.
attribution: Terrain: Terrain Tiles (AWS Open Data / Mapzen), including data from SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1, EU-DEM (Copernicus) and national LIDAR sources

axes: metres; x east, y up, z south (-z is north); y = 0 is the plot's mean ground level

terrain.encoding: float32le, row-major, rows run +z (north to south), columns run +x (west to east)

factors.label: Sloping site
factors.detail: Falls about 44% to the south-east, 31.5 m across the plot. Expect cut and fill, retaining walls or stepped foundations.

factors.label: Road or path crosses the plot
factors.detail: Crossed by Victoria Terrace. It must be diverted or kept open.

factors.label: Awkward plot shape
factors.detail: Irregular outline (fills 60% of its bounding rectangle).

factors.label: Tight access
factors.detail: Access is by a single road. Limits crane and delivery sizes.

factors.label: Existing buildings to clear
factors.detail: 1 building(s) (30 m2 of footprint) stand on the plot and must be demolished and cleared first.

factors.label: Made ground
factors.detail: Previously developed land: buried foundations, fill and possible contamination. Trial pits recommended.
